cautions: Never offer Obatala alcohol (including palm wine), palm oil, salt, or hot pepper — these are among his best-known taboos.

Offerings and practices vary widely across lineages and houses; always seek guidance from an initiated practitioner or elder before approaching Obatala. Avoid attempting restricted rites without proper initiation.

Specific colors, rhythms, and offerings differ by lineage. Ceremonial work with Yemaya should be undertaken only with proper guidance from a trained practitioner. Avoid restricted rites without initiation.

Shango's rites are highly initiatory and lineage-specific. Ceremonial drumming and specific offerings require the oversight of a knowledgeable elder or priest/priestess. Avoid restricted rites without initiation.

ritualObjects: Iron tools — hammer, anvil, machete, hoe, pick
cautions: Offerings to Ogun, particularly animal offerings, are strictly lineage-dependent. Consult an initiated practitioner before working with Ogun. Avoid restricted rites without initiation.

ritualObjects: Otá — consecrated stone or cement head with cowrie-shell eyes
cautions: Eshu (also known as Elegguá or Elegba in related traditions) must always be acknowledged first in ceremony. Approaches to Eshu are highly tradition-specific. Consult a knowledgeable practitioner and avoid restricted rites without initiation.
Honey should be tasted before offering to Oshun in traditional practice; always research lineage-specific protocols. Avoid restricted rites without guidance from an initiated practitioner.

Ifá divination is a sacred and highly specialized practice requiring years of study and initiation. Do not attempt to conduct Ifá divination without proper training. Consult a trained babalawo or iyanifa for guidance.

symbolism: The passage between life and death
ritualObjects: Maroon beads striped black and white
cautions: Many houses forbid ram (mutton) around Oya.

Oya's connection to the dead and the cemetery means her ceremonies require great care and lineage-specific knowledge. Do not approach cemetery or mortuary rites without initiation and elder guidance. Avoid restricted rites without initiation.

Orunmila is closely identified with the Ifá oracle. Ceremonial and divinatory approaches require initiation and training. Consult a trained babalawo for Ifá-related guidance. Avoid restricted rites without proper initiation.
Ochosi is received with the Warriors (Elegguá, Ogún, Ochosi, Osun) through initiation. Consult an initiated practitioner before working with him.

commonOfferings: A gourd of black beans topped with a red onion
cautions: Babalú-Ayé is approached with great respect; his rites and the pilgrimage to El Rincón are serious devotional acts. Consult an initiated practitioner before working with him.
Osain is received and worked by initiated herbalists (osainistas and babalawos). Consult an initiated practitioner before working with him.
Olokun of Ifá is given by babalawos, and Olokun is never crowned on an initiate’s head. Consult an initiated practitioner; do not attempt his rites alone.
Practices around twins and the Ibeji differ by region and house. Consult an initiated practitioner before approaching their rites.
Aganju is received through initiation in Lucumí practice. Consult an initiated practitioner before working with him.
Oba is received through initiation, and many houses rarely crown her. Consult an initiated practitioner before working with her.
Yewá is served with strict modesty and is traditionally tended by elders; her taboos are severe. Consult an initiated practitioner before approaching her.
